1	/**
2	 * Maps one Recently Viewed product onto the subset of `ZimmProductCard` props the
3	 * `recentlyViewed` variation (SFCC-83) actually renders.
4	 *
5	 * **Input source revised 2026-09-08 (build plan §2, "Interim data source") — Einstein is "Not
6	 * Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site, so this build ships against a browser-tracked
7	 * view-history stand-in instead.** Input is now a plain Commerce API `Product`
8	 * (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`), exactly as returned by
9	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own `getProducts` call (`expand: [
10	 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`, `allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`) —
11	 * the same underlying Shopper Products shape the original Einstein-sourced design used, minus the
12	 * Einstein-specific `rec`/flat-`image` wrapper fields `fetchRecProductDetails`
13	 * (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505`) used to bolt on. This
14	 * mapper's own output contract and scope (image-only, no gallery, no was/now pricing — A2's
15	 * `recentlyViewed` variation decision, unchanged) are unaffected; only the shape of what it reads
16	 * on the way in changed, and with it, `selectPrimaryImage`'s fallback below: there is no longer a
17	 * separate flat Einstein image to fall back to, so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no
18	 * usable `src`" and "there is no usable image at all" are now the same case.
19	 *
20	 * Modelled on `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — no React/react-intl import,
21	 * `formatPrice` injected as a parameter so this module stays independently testable — and on the
22	 * general shape of `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (`feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, not this
23	 * branch — read for its approach, not imported). Unlike that demo mapper, this is a production
24	 * path: real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` SDK types are used directly (AGENTS.md > Type
25	 * Definitions) — with the Einstein-specific input shape gone, there is no longer any hand-rolled
26	 * field on the input type at all.
27	 *
28	 * Deliberately narrow scope, stated here rather than left as a silent gap: this mapper only ever
29	 * returns `currentPrice` (an active selling price), not was/now sale-price detection
30	 * (`originalPrice`) — but that is a scope choice, not a data limitation. **Correction
31	 * (2026-09-08, pre-dates and is unaffected by the input-source revision above):** an earlier
32	 * version of this comment claimed the merged Einstein shape "has no equivalent of"
33	 * `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic — verified inaccurate, and equally true of the plain
34	 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads: `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` already requests
35	 * `perPricebook: true`, so `product.tieredPrices` is present, and base SFCC's `getPriceData`
36	 * (`app/utils/product-utils.js`) already derives `listPrice`/`isOnSale` from exactly that field —
37	 * nothing is missing, it's simply not called here. The real reason `originalPrice` isn't mapped is
38	 * that the `recentlyViewed` variation renders no price at all today (see
39	 * `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row — `showContent: false`), so
40	 * there is nothing for it to feed. Mapping `currentPrice` anyway costs nothing and means a future
41	 * consumer of this same mapper (e.g. a variation that does render price) isn't blocked on this
42	 * file being revisited — extending it to also call `getPriceData` at that point would be a small,
43	 * well-precedented addition, not new pricebook work.
44	 */
45	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
46	import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
47	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
48	import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
49	import { sortImagesBySequence, resolveFallbackColour, resolveRequiredAlt } from './productCardMappingHelpers';
50	
51	/**
52	 * The real Commerce API `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
53	 * — not hand-rolled). A plain alias, not an augmentation: unlike the pre-revision Einstein-sourced
54	 * shape this replaces, `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s plain `getProducts` result needs nothing
55	 * bolted on — `Product.id` is used directly, and there is no separate flat-image field. Kept as a
56	 * named alias (rather than importing `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` directly at each call site)
57	 * so this module's own input type has a name that documents its role here.
58	 */
59	export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product;
60	
61	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
62	 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
63	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
64	
65	/**
66	 * The subset of `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` this mapper populates. Deliberately excludes
67	 * `headingLevel` and `variation` — both are render-context decisions belonging to the container
68	 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies
69	 * `headingLevel` uniformly for every card and adds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` itself when
70	 * spreading this output into `<ZimmProductCard>` — the rail organism itself (A5) takes already-full
71	 * `ZimmProductCardProps` objects, so variation must already be set before it sees them. A pure data
72	 * mapper choosing a heading level would conflate a data concern with a layout one. Also excludes `hoverImage`/`images` — this
73	 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
74	 * for why.
75	 */
76	export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
77	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
78	  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
79	>;
80	
81	/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
82	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's
83	 *  no-magic-strings rule — this is a real, semantic SFCC image `viewType` key. */
84	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
85	
86	/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
87	 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */
88	const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
89	
90	/** The one shape this mapper sorts — whatever `ImageGroup.images` actually holds. */
91	type ImageGroupImage = NonNullable<ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup['images']>[number];
92	
93	/**
94	 * Sorts by the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into each image's own filename
95	 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`) — confirmed live on `4673TS251`,
96	 * whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`, which silently showed the on-model
97	 * shot (image `2`) as primary instead of the flat-lay shot (always image `1`).
98	 *
99	 * Shared with `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — see
100	 * `productCardMappingHelpers.ts`'s own docblock for why a shared primitive rather than three
101	 * separate copies (all three had drifted onto the identical non-transitive-comparator bug,
102	 * CodeRabbit 2026-09-10). This file's own images are the raw SDK shape (`disBaseLink`/`link`,
103	 * not a flat `src`), hence the explicit accessor.
104	 */
105	const sortByImageSequence = (images: ImageGroupImage[]): ImageGroupImage[] =>
106	  sortImagesBySequence(images, (image) => image.disBaseLink || image.link || '');
107	
108	/**
109	 * Resolves which real colour this product's one image should come from — now the shared
110	 * `resolveFallbackColour` (`productCardMappingHelpers.ts`) directly, since there is no
111	 * `representedProduct` branch to add here: this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
112	 * (from `getProducts`), which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type).
113	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` layers exactly one extra branch
114	 * (a `representedProduct` match, Search-hit-only) in front of this same shared fallback.
115	 * Returns `undefined` when there are no variants at all — `selectPrimaryImage` below then falls
116	 * back to an unscoped, viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
117	 */
118	const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct): string | undefined =>
119	  resolveFallbackColour(product.variants, COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
120	
121	/**
122	 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
123	 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
124	 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
125	 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
126	 * `images` at all).
127	 *
128	 * Uses `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image),
129	 * **colour-scoped first, then viewtype-only as a fallback** — same two-pass fix, same reasoning,
130	 * as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectColourScopedImages`, closing a real bug confirmed
131	 * live on `4673TS251`: with no colour scoping at all, an older, untagged, genuinely-404 medium
132	 * group and a newer, correctly colour-tagged one are both candidates, and the untagged one wins by
133	 * default purely because it happens to sit first in the API's own array order. Scoping by colour
134	 * excludes the untagged group outright. The fallback pass exists for the opposite real case — a
135	 * genuinely single-colour product whose one medium group carries no `variationAttributes` tag at
136	 * all (nothing to disambiguate) — which a strict colour-scoped lookup alone would exclude and
137	 * return nothing for. Never the reverse: a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
138	 * avoid re-mixing colours.
139	 *
140	 * **No flat-image fallback (2026-09-08 input-source revision).** The pre-revision Einstein-merged
141	 * shape carried its own flat `image.disBaseLink`/`image.alt` (Einstein's own single-reference
142	 * thumbnail) to fall back to when `imageGroups` filtering came up empty. The plain
143	 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads has no equivalent field at all — `imageGroups` is the
144	 * only image source there is — so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no usable `src`" and
145	 * "there is no usable image at all" have collapsed into the same case; both now return `null`.
146	 *
147	 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
148	 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image — "no usable
149	 *   image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard
150	 *   gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null` here is the only option that structurally
151	 *   cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since there is no returned object for `alt` to
152	 *   be empty on.
153	 */
154	const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
155	  const colour = resolveViewedColour(product);
156	
157	  const colourScopedGroups = colour
158	    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
159	        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
160	        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
161	      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
162	    : [];
163	
164	  const groups =
165	    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
166	      ? colourScopedGroups
167	      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
168	          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
169	        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);
170	
171	  const [groupImage] = sortByImageSequence(groups[0]?.images ?? []);
172	  if (!groupImage) return null;
173	
174	  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
175	  if (!src) return null;
176	
177	  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
178	  // decorative alt: '' convention) — shared resolveRequiredAlt (productCardMappingHelpers.ts).
179	  const alt = resolveRequiredAlt(groupImage.alt, productName);
180	  return { src, alt };
181	};
182	
183	/**
184	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
185	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
186	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
187	 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the product
188	 *   has no usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw.

/**
 * Maps one Recently Viewed product onto the subset of `ZimmProductCard` props the
 * `recentlyViewed` variation (SFCC-83) actually renders.
 *
 * **Input source revised 2026-09-08 (build plan §2, "Interim data source") — Einstein is "Not
 * Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site, so this build ships against a browser-tracked
 * view-history stand-in instead.** Input is now a plain Commerce API `Product`
 * (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`), exactly as returned by
 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own `getProducts` call (`expand: [
 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`, `allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`) —
 * the same underlying Shopper Products shape the original Einstein-sourced design used, minus the
 * Einstein-specific `rec`/flat-`image` wrapper fields `fetchRecProductDetails`
 * (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505`) used to bolt on. This
 * mapper's own output contract and scope (image-only, no gallery, no was/now pricing — A2's
 * `recentlyViewed` variation decision, unchanged) are unaffected; only the shape of what it reads
 * on the way in changed, and with it, `selectPrimaryImage`'s fallback below: there is no longer a
 * separate flat Einstein image to fall back to, so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no
 * usable `src`" and "there is no usable image at all" are now the same case.
 *
 * Modelled on `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — no React/react-intl import,
 * `formatPrice` injected as a parameter so this module stays independently testable — and on the
 * general shape of `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (`feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, not this
 * branch — read for its approach, not imported). Unlike that demo mapper, this is a production
 * path: real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` SDK types are used directly (AGENTS.md > Type
 * Definitions) — with the Einstein-specific input shape gone, there is no longer any hand-rolled
 * field on the input type at all.
 *
 * Deliberately narrow scope, stated here rather than left as a silent gap: this mapper only ever
 * returns `currentPrice` (an active selling price), not was/now sale-price detection
 * (`originalPrice`) — but that is a scope choice, not a data limitation. **Correction
 * (2026-09-08, pre-dates and is unaffected by the input-source revision above):** an earlier
 * version of this comment claimed the merged Einstein shape "has no equivalent of"
 * `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic — verified inaccurate, and equally true of the plain
 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads: `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` already requests
 * `perPricebook: true`, so `product.tieredPrices` is present, and base SFCC's `getPriceData`
 * (`app/utils/product-utils.js`) already derives `listPrice`/`isOnSale` from exactly that field —
 * nothing is missing, it's simply not called here. The real reason `originalPrice` isn't mapped is
 * that the `recentlyViewed` variation renders no price at all today (see
 * `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row — `showContent: false`), so
 * there is nothing for it to feed. Mapping `currentPrice` anyway costs nothing and means a future
 * consumer of this same mapper (e.g. a variation that does render price) isn't blocked on this
 * file being revisited — extending it to also call `getPriceData` at that point would be a small,
 * well-precedented addition, not new pricebook work.
 */
import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
import { sortImagesBySequence, resolveFallbackColour, resolveRequiredAlt } from './productCardMappingHelpers';

/**
 * The real Commerce API `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
 * — not hand-rolled). A plain alias, not an augmentation: unlike the pre-revision Einstein-sourced
 * shape this replaces, `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s plain `getProducts` result needs nothing
 * bolted on — `Product.id` is used directly, and there is no separate flat-image field. Kept as a
 * named alias (rather than importing `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` directly at each call site)
 * so this module's own input type has a name that documents its role here.
 */
export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product;

/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;

/**
 * The subset of `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` this mapper populates. Deliberately excludes
 * `headingLevel` and `variation` — both are render-context decisions belonging to the container
 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies
 * `headingLevel` uniformly for every card and adds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` itself when
 * spreading this output into `<ZimmProductCard>` — the rail organism itself (A5) takes already-full
 * `ZimmProductCardProps` objects, so variation must already be set before it sees them. A pure data
 * mapper choosing a heading level would conflate a data concern with a layout one. Also excludes `hoverImage`/`images` — this
 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
 * for why.
 */
export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
>;

/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's
 *  no-magic-strings rule — this is a real, semantic SFCC image `viewType` key. */
const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';

/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */
const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';

/** The one shape this mapper sorts — whatever `ImageGroup.images` actually holds. */
type ImageGroupImage = NonNullable<ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup['images']>[number];

/**
 * Sorts by the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into each image's own filename
 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`) — confirmed live on `4673TS251`,
 * whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`, which silently showed the on-model
 * shot (image `2`) as primary instead of the flat-lay shot (always image `1`).
 *
 * Shared with `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — see
 * `productCardMappingHelpers.ts`'s own docblock for why a shared primitive rather than three
 * separate copies (all three had drifted onto the identical non-transitive-comparator bug,
 * CodeRabbit 2026-09-10). This file's own images are the raw SDK shape (`disBaseLink`/`link`,
 * not a flat `src`), hence the explicit accessor.
 */
const sortByImageSequence = (images: ImageGroupImage[]): ImageGroupImage[] =>
  sortImagesBySequence(images, (image) => image.disBaseLink || image.link || '');

/**
 * Resolves which real colour this product's one image should come from — now the shared
 * `resolveFallbackColour` (`productCardMappingHelpers.ts`) directly, since there is no
 * `representedProduct` branch to add here: this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
 * (from `getProducts`), which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type).
 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` layers exactly one extra branch
 * (a `representedProduct` match, Search-hit-only) in front of this same shared fallback.
 * Returns `undefined` when there are no variants at all — `selectPrimaryImage` below then falls
 * back to an unscoped, viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
 */
const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct): string | undefined =>
  resolveFallbackColour(product.variants, COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);

/**
 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
 * `images` at all).
 *
 * Uses `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image),
 * **colour-scoped first, then viewtype-only as a fallback** — same two-pass fix, same reasoning,
 * as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectColourScopedImages`, closing a real bug confirmed
 * live on `4673TS251`: with no colour scoping at all, an older, untagged, genuinely-404 medium
 * group and a newer, correctly colour-tagged one are both candidates, and the untagged one wins by
 * default purely because it happens to sit first in the API's own array order. Scoping by colour
 * excludes the untagged group outright. The fallback pass exists for the opposite real case — a
 * genuinely single-colour product whose one medium group carries no `variationAttributes` tag at
 * all (nothing to disambiguate) — which a strict colour-scoped lookup alone would exclude and
 * return nothing for. Never the reverse: a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
 * avoid re-mixing colours.
 *
 * **No flat-image fallback (2026-09-08 input-source revision).** The pre-revision Einstein-merged
 * shape carried its own flat `image.disBaseLink`/`image.alt` (Einstein's own single-reference
 * thumbnail) to fall back to when `imageGroups` filtering came up empty. The plain
 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads has no equivalent field at all — `imageGroups` is the
 * only image source there is — so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no usable `src`" and
 * "there is no usable image at all" have collapsed into the same case; both now return `null`.
 *
 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image — "no usable
 *   image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard
 *   gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null` here is the only option that structurally
 *   cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since there is no returned object for `alt` to
 *   be empty on.
 */
const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
  const colour = resolveViewedColour(product);

  const colourScopedGroups = colour
    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
    : [];

  const groups =
    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
      ? colourScopedGroups
      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);

  const [groupImage] = sortByImageSequence(groups[0]?.images ?? []);
  if (!groupImage) return null;

  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
  if (!src) return null;

  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
  // decorative alt: '' convention) — shared resolveRequiredAlt (productCardMappingHelpers.ts).
  const alt = resolveRequiredAlt(groupImage.alt, productName);
  return { src, alt };
};

/**
 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the product
 *   has no usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw.
 */
export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {
  if (!product?.name) return null;

  const primaryImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
  if (!primaryImage) return null;

  return {
    id: product.id,
    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
    name: product.name,
    primaryImage,
    // No hardcoded fallback currency — if either is absent, skip formatting rather than guess,
    // matching productInfo.ts's own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment.
    currentPrice:
      typeof product.price === 'number' && product.currency ? formatPrice(product.price, product.currency) : undefined,
  };
};

content.text:
E4 is done. Branch confirmed as `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein` (not `develop`/`main`) before touching anything.

## What this step means, in one line

The two interim "Recently Viewed" files (browser-storage tracking + its product-fetch helper) are gone, every comment anywhere in `overrides/` that talked about them as if they were still alive or "coming soon to be deleted" now says the truthful thing, and the app still compiles and tests green. Five stale comment mentions remain on purpose, inside three files your own task message told me not to touch — flagged below, not silently left.

## What I deleted

- `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`
- `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.test.ts`
- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`
- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.test.ts`

Filenames confirmed exact via `find` before deleting (no mismatch with the task's names). Before deleting, I grepped all of `overrides/` for both module names and found only comment-only references outside the modules' own files and tests — no live import anywhere (double-checked specifically for `from '.*useRecentlyViewedHistory'` / `from '.*recentlyViewedProductFetch'`, both empty outside the two `.test.ts` files that imported their own module). No undisclosed consumer existed.

## Constants — removed vs. kept, and why the "kept" question doesn't quite apply

Only **`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`** actually lived in `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` (line 18) — I removed it and its explanatory comment block (`overrides/app/constants/index.ts`, was lines 11–18), after confirming its only remaining references anywhere were comments (in `recommended-products/index.tsx`, `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx` + its stories, `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`), all swept below.

**`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_STORAGE_KEY`** and **`GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST`** were never in `constants/index.ts` at all — the first was `export const`-defined inside `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` itself, the second was a local (non-exported) const inside `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`, derived from the constant above. Both vanished automatically when I deleted those two files in step 1. There was no separate "remove from constants/index.ts" edit to make for either — I verified this by grepping the whole repo (not just `overrides/`) for each of the three names individually before touching anything, per the task's instruction.

## Comment sweep — exact before/after

**`overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`** (2 spots):
- Lines ~46–51: `"both deleted in build plan step E4"` → `"both removed in build plan step E4"` (was asserting a completed action before E4 had run; now true).
- Lines ~361–367 (the `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED, 24` cap claim): reworded to `cards.length` reflecting Einstein's `recommendations.recs` directly with no client-side cap, citing Open Question 4.

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx`** (~line 62, `cards` JSDoc): removed the claim that the page container "caps its fetch at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`" — replaced with "forwards whatever Einstein's own `recommendations.recs` returns — no client-side cap."

**`.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.stories.tsx`** (~line 199, `ManyItems` docblock): reworded from "24 cards — the real, designed ceiling for this surface... caps its own fetch/display at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`" to "an illustrative 'many items' volume, not a designed ceiling." Left the actual `buildCards(24)` args/assertions untouched — comment-only, per your do-not-touch on component/story logic.

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`** (~line 91): `` `useRecentlyViewedHistory` / `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` `` → "Einstein's own `recommendations.recs`, wired in build plan step E1." (Not one of your 4 named locations, but plan.md's own E4 sweep list names this file, and it literally contained both deleted-file names, so the zero-hit grep would fail without it.)

**`overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`** (2 spots — one beyond the named ~278):
- Lines ~174–180 docblock: `"scheduled for deletion in build plan step E4, not yet run as of this commit... the files still exist on disk pending that step"` → `"removed in build plan step E4... the files themselves are now gone too."` This wasn't in your named list, but it's the same "future tense about E4" pattern as the recommended-products spot, and now that E4 has actually run, leaving it unfixed would mean the docblock says something false about the very deletion this commit performs. I fixed it for the same reason, not as scope creep.
- Line ~315 (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED real <h3>...`): reworded to "however many real `<h3>` product-name headings ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid renders (uncapped as of build plan step E4)."

**`overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts`** (docblock-only — verified via diff, every changed line is inside a `/** */` or `//` comment): reworded its 4 stale `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` citations to describe "the interim build's own dedicated fetch utility" historically, and added the plan's optional note ("Superseded 2026-09-15... input is once again the Einstein rec") confirming no functional change was needed — matching finding #11's superset reasoning already established for the full-history mapper.

## What I deliberately did NOT touch, and the one real conflict this leaves open

Your task named `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` and `recentlyViewedCard.test.ts` as do-not-touch (the latter "unless the plan explicitly names a change" — it doesn't, for either test file). I extended that same protection to `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts` as a sibling test file already-committed outside this step's remit. plan.md's own text is inconsistent here — it separately says "no change" to `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`/`.test.ts` **and** says E4 should "sweep stale comment references... in... the two mapper files." I followed your more specific, directly-given instruction over the plan's looser phrasing.

**Consequence:** the final grep is not literally zero. Five hits remain, all comment-only, all inside the three protected files:
```
overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:6, 105, 352   → `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`
overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts:2        → `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`
overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.test.ts:2                   → `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`
```
This is Marcel's call, not mine, per the instructions I'm operating under — I did not silently edit a file you named off-limits, and I'm not silently claiming the pass criterion is met when it isn't. If a follow-up sweep of these three is wanted, it's a 5-line comment-only edit; if finding #11's "no change" ruling on this file was meant to be absolute, no action needed.

**Separately, out of scope entirely:** `.claude/registry/hooks.md` and `.claude/registry/utils.md` (both headed "Generated by `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — do not edit manually") still list `useRecentlyViewedHistory` and `recentlyViewedProductFetch` as if they exist. Not named in my file manifest, auto-generated, so I left them alone — worth a `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` re-run at some point, not urgent.

## Evidence for each pass criterion

- **Zero-hit grep across `overrides/`, comments included** — not fully zero; see above (5 hits, 3 protected files, flagged for your ratification).
- **`recentlyViewedCard.ts` diff is docblock-only** — confirmed: `git diff` shows every `+`/`-` line starts with `*` or `//`; same check run across all 5 other comment-edited files, same result (zero non-comment lines touched anywhere except the deliberate constant removal in `constants/index.ts`).
- **`npx tsc --noEmit`** — exit 0, no output.
- **`npm run test`** — `Test Files 85 passed (85)`, `Tests 1305 passed (1305)`. (Console noise about `MISSING_TRANSLATION` for `recently_viewed.*` message ids is pre-existing test-environment behaviour, not a failure — the test file itself passed.) `recipeGuards.test.ts` (the styling gate) passed — expected, since this step made zero styling/token changes.
- **`npm run lint`** — 8 errors / 43 warnings, all in files I never touched this session (`_app/index.tsx`, `drawer-menu/*`, `header/rightBar/index.tsx`, `product-view/index.tsx`, `zimmSocialButton`, `zimmTextInput`, `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer`, `useHeaderNav.ts`, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, `product-detail/index.tsx`, `product-list/index.tsx`). Zero in any file I edited or deleted — no new errors introduced.
- **`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`** — 3 unacknowledged raw-value findings (`footer.css.ts`, `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts`) — all pre-existing, none in a file I touched. No new findings.
- **`npm run build`** — exit 0. Warnings only (pre-existing `@contentful/experiences-components-react` source-map ENOENT noise, and a pre-existing `core-polyfill.js` bundle-size warning) — none related to my change.
- **Post-build translations/compiled discard** — `build-translations` regenerated `translations/en-GB.json`, `translations/en-US.json`, and 4 files under `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/`. I inspected the diff: it's unrelated message-catalog drift (`gallery_overlay.*` additions, `header.*` reordering) with nothing from Recently Viewed in it — confirming it's the documented pre-existing side effect, not something my change caused. **I could not discard it myself** — my operating constraints for this task prohibit `git checkout`/`restore`/`stash` under any circumstance. These 6 files are left modified in the working tree; whoever stages this step's commit should exclude `translations/` and `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/` from it.
